1n5bzje.200: Small agricultural municipality of Lomellina, the plain between Ticino, Po and Sesia; around the medieval castle, with the south facade of the eighteenth-century villa, is the Museum of art and peasant tradition.
zf3onf.522: Set up in a restored rural building, once a barn and barn, in the estate of the medieval castle, it collects about 2,500 pieces of the world of Lomellino peasant from the nineteenth century to the sixties of the twentieth century: tools for the breeding of cattle and pigs, wagons, ploughs, furniture and agricultural machinery. The route is divided into five areas: agricultural work cycle, domestic life environments, ancient crafts artisans, stable and courtyard, heavy agricultural machinery; remarkable reconstructions of rural environments.

Boat excursions of about an hour and a half with Navigare Fiume Po (€15 per person on October 11, 2026, mandatory booking) start from the pier of the village of San Pietro.

q5s0mn.329: Small agricultural town of Lomellina dominated by an imposing castle with shelter, one of the most significant fortified complexes of the province of Pavia, where they stayed Isabella d'Aragona, Massimiliano I of Habsburg and Carlo V; inside the Strada family preserves an archaeological museum with finds of the Lomellina.
1zjdmn.672: Castello e ricetto, a building type unique in Lombardy and spread in the nearby Piedmont: the nucleus probably dates back to the X-XII centuries; in 1404 the Folperti obtained from the Visconti to expand it and build the ricetto, then passed to the Malaspina (with portico and loggia of the fifteenth century) and in 1582 to Cardinal Tolomeo Gallio, who had built chapel, garden and stables. Visconti plant with courtyard and well in brick, battlements, corner towers, moat and barbacan with drawbridge; inside Renaissance fireplaces, loggia of Bramante style and 19th century rooms. ==References====External links==* Official website
